edits.before:
do not substitute another job, head, claim id, public fence or session label.

  Only `authorize_head` accepts optional `terminal_release_ready`. Set it to `true` only when the actual holder has finished all editing in these exact current resources and explicitly permits conditional release after every associated PR reliably terminates and execution is proved idle. The service records that intent in an immutable existing Receipt; a head SHA in `progress_ref` alone is never this declaration. `false`, a later successful authorization that omits the field, key reissue, changed resources, renewal or handover invalidates prior readiness. Do not treat CI's read permission or a public session label as holder intent. Read-only claim verification reports `terminal_release_ready`; this conditional intent neither ends a Task nor grants execution or production permission.

edits.before:
Preserve the `terminal_admission` object actually returned by a full successful Native CI admission, including its immutable receipt id, claim id, fence, execution epoch, lease version and exact head-authorization id. Carry it through the protected existing batch/landing record; never fabricate a last-admission witness from the current resolver or select a newer generation by timestamp. Trusted close/merge handling uses only the existing terminal/adopt/return entry and a fresh real closed observation for the exact repository, PR, head and target. The admission retains the base actually admitted; the terminal observation may report the now-advanced base. Code already present on main while its PR remains open is ordinary adoption, not proof of a closed PR. Preserve the existing race-winner rules.

  Automatic claim release requires the original holder's still-valid readiness, exact last-admission resources and generation CAS, every PR terminal across repositories, and positively established runtime idle. Any active or unknown PR, undiscovered authorization, unfinished editing or broad/incompletely covered write set, current or old unsettled execution/publication/dispatch, or pending handover keeps the claim. Never infer idle from an empty Native table, a completed check, or a same-head old stop Receipt. Missing complete all-events runtime inventory returns `runtime_inventory_unconfirmed`; this successor also leaves every nonempty external run inventory unsupported with `physical_execution_unconfirmed` until exact per-attempt physical-stop qualification exists. Do not forge an empty inventory, borrow another consumer's credential or change App permissions to bypass that boundary. The original immutable release Receipt retains the actual terminal observation, original admission reference and runtime evidence digest/provenance. A pending outcome keeps the existing landing record retryable with its original proof; a retained/refused outcome must state its reason, never success. Closure of one PR cannot release another PR's work, close the business Task or revive an obsolete key/epoch. Where evidence is unavailable, retain the claim and report the limitation; the ordinary existing holder/Owner closeout rules remain available.
edits.after: When qualified CI ends a pull request's Task binding (adopt when it merged, return when it closed), the service releases the claim that served that pull request as `completed`, with the pull request as `evidence_ref`, when both hold: the Task has no other open pull request, and the claim authorized no newer head after its last authorization or CI admission of that pull request. Otherwise the claim stays and you release it as usual. You need not release a claim released this way. To go on with the Task, claim it again: within 15 minutes of that release the new claim continues the old one and takes no token ([Appendix A.8](#appendix-a8)).
